outputs.L1: The variable-magnification optical system comprises: a positive first lens group G1 disposed closest to the object side; a negative intermediate group G2 disposed on the image side of the first lens group G1; a positive focusing group G3 disposed on the image side of the intermediate group G2 and configured to move during focusing; and a positive image-side group G4 disposed on the image side of the focusing group G3. During magnification variation, the distances between the first lens group G1 and the intermediate group G2, between the intermediate group G2 and the focusing group G3, and between the focusing group G3 and the image-side group G4 are varied, while a predetermined conditional expression is satisfied. This configuration provides a variable-magnification optical system having excellent optical performance and a reduced-weight focusing lens group that enables high-speed focusing operation, among other advantages.
outputs.L2: The variable-magnification optical system includes, in order from the object side, a first lens group G1 with positive refractive power, an intermediate lens group G2 with negative refractive power, a focusing lens group G3 with positive refractive power, and an image-side lens group G4 with positive refractive power. Focusing is performed by moving G3. During magnification changes, the separations between G1 and G2, between G2 and G3, and between G3 and G4 are each adjusted. The system also satisfies a specified conditional expression. This configuration provides excellent optical performance while reducing the weight of the focusing lens group, thereby enabling high-speed focusing and other benefits.
outputs.L3: The optical system includes, in order from the object side toward the image side, a first lens group having positive refractive power, an intermediate lens group having negative refractive power, a focusing lens group having positive refractive power, and an image-side lens group having positive refractive power. During focusing, the focusing lens group moves along the optical axis, while magnification is varied by changing the axial distances between adjacent lens groups. The optical system is configured to satisfy a predetermined optical condition that appropriately balances refractive power and lens-group arrangement. This configuration provides strong optical performance throughout the magnification range while enabling high-speed focusing through the use of a compact, lightweight focusing lens group.
outputs.L4:
A variable-magnification optical system is arranged, in order from the object side to the image side, with a first lens group having positive refractive power, a second lens group having negative refractive power, a third lens group having positive refractive power, and a fourth lens group having positive refractive power. During a change in magnification, the distances between adjacent lens groups are varied in a prescribed manner. Focusing is performed by moving the third lens group along the optical axis, while the other lens groups remain stationary or move according to the magnification operation.

The refractive powers, focal lengths, and movement characteristics of the lens groups are selected to satisfy a specified optical condition. This arrangement effectively corrects aberrations throughout the magnification range and maintains high imaging performance from infinity to close-focus distances. Because the movable focusing group is compact and lightweight, the load placed on the focusing drive mechanism is reduced. The system therefore achieves rapid, accurate focusing while retaining excellent optical performance across the full variable-magnification range.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a variable-magnification optical system with four lens groups, including a lightweight focusing group for high-speed autofocus.
counterfactuals.output: A variable-magnification optical system includes, in order from an object side to an image side, first, second, third, and fourth lens groups having respective refractive powers. Magnification is varied by changing at least two inter-group spacings through movement of one or more of the lens groups along an optical axis. At least one lens group is configured as a focusing group movable along the optical axis to perform focusing from an infinite-distance object to a finite-distance object. The focusing group includes a reduced number of compact lens elements and has a mass lower than that of each adjacent movable lens group, thereby reducing drive load and enabling high-speed autofocus. The refractive powers, lens configurations, and movement trajectories of the four lens groups are selected to suppress aberration fluctuations during zooming and focusing while maintaining image quality over a variable-magnification range. The system is suitable for use in an imaging apparatus requiring compactness, rapid focus response, and reduced power consumption.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical summary of an optical system in which the spacings among four lens groups vary during magnification and a predetermined conditional expression ensures excellent optical performance.
counterfactuals.output: The optical system is a zoom lens comprising four lens groups arranged sequentially along the optical axis. During magnification, the groups move relative to one another so that the axial spacings between adjacent groups vary, thereby changing the system focal length while maintaining image formation at a substantially fixed image plane. The refractive powers, focal lengths, and/or movement amounts of selected groups are configured to satisfy a predetermined conditional expression. This relationship constrains the optical-power distribution and zooming geometry, suppressing aberration fluctuations—particularly spherical aberration, coma, astigmatism, distortion, and chromatic aberration—throughout the magnification range. As a result, the system achieves a compact configuration, effective zoom operation, and consistently high optical performance from the wide-angle end to the telephoto end.
